The LSE site and Yahoo Finance history could not be retrieved (page failed to render / HTTP 503). 4,664.50p (Trading Economics) is used because it is the only source that states an explicit 25 Sep close. CURRENCY: the model reports in EUR (valuation_inputs.json currency_unit = EURm) and ULVR trades in GBX; any comparison needs an explicit GBP/EUR conversion. Also, MarketScreener's EUR target is not the same as TipRanks' GBX target, and MarketBeat's figure is for the USD ADR. Of the three, only TipRanks is in the ULVR listing's own currency, so it is the primary consensus. The three consensus aggregators give different rating labels (Moderate Buy / Outperform / Hold) and analyst counts (10 / 16 / 12). The fair summary is 'mildly positive to neutral, roughly 7-13% upside to the mean target'. HYPERINFLATION TREATMENT IN ANALYST COMMENTARY (the key question): no sell-side note or analyst question was found that separates the IAS 29 net monetary gain/(loss) from ordinary FX translation. (1) Q2 2026 earnings call, 2026-07-28/29 (Motley Fool transcript, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/29/unilever-ul-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/): Argentina comes up only as an operating story. CEO Fernando Fernandez: 'In the second quarter, Argentina delivered high single-digit volume growth'. Currency is discussed only as an aggregate translation effect. CFO Srinivas Phatak: 'Currency reduced our first half turnover by 4.9%... that impact eased materially to 2.4% in the quarter', 'Currency reduced the underlying EPS growth by around 6 percentage points in the first half', 'Based on July spot rates, we expect the full year impact to be around 3%.' There is no mention of Türkiye, IAS 29, or the net monetary gain/loss, and no analyst asked about them. (2) Q1 2026 call (Investing.com transcript, https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-unilevers-q1-2026-reveals-strong-volume-growth-93CH-4647991): CEO: 'in Argentina, high single digit growth'; 'strong performances in markets such as India, Turkey, and Vietnam'. CFO: 'FX reducing the reported turnover by 7.7%'. Again there is no mention of hyperinflation accounting or the monetary gain/loss. (3) Press coverage of the consensus (ad-hoc-news/MarketBeat, TipRanks' summary) mentions bears citing 'foreign exchange headwinds' in general and never IAS 29. (4) Unilever's own framing in its H1 2026 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000217410/000021741026000057/ul-20260630.htm) and its USG methodology documents deals with hyperinflation mainly by capping hyperinflationary price growth in underlying sales growth: 'price growth in excess of 26% per year in hyperinflationary economies has been excluded when calculating the underlying sales growth'. The net monetary line appears in the income statement but does not feature in the call narrative. CONCLUSION: this supports the [PLACEHOLDER] hypothesis in valuation_inputs.json's consensus.note. The IAS 29 net monetary gain/(loss) is effectively treated as a non-cash item below the underlying measures and ignored.
